_metadata.description: Biomarker → tissue-level [S]/Km mapping for each Tier 2 lifestyle multiplier.
_metadata.context: v6 Methods / Exposure integration module: 'The complete mapping of Tier 2 lifestyle multipliers to their primary biomarker data sources, published concentration ranges, and derived [S]/Km ratios.'

schema.biomarker: Urinary / blood / serum biomarker used for reverse dosimetry
schema.matrix: Biospecimen matrix measured (urine, whole_blood, serum, plasma, exhaled_breath)
schema.reference_range: Published population central range for the biomarker
schema.partition_coefficient: Matrix→tissue conversion factor used in the PBPK step
schema.target_enzyme: Primary metabolizing enzyme whose Km is used for normalization
schema.Km_uM: Km value used in the denominator of the [S]/Km ratio
schema.S_over_Km_central: Central [S]/Km ratio used by the interaction / flux engines at Tier 2 baseline
schema.S_over_Km_range: Minimum and maximum [S]/Km ratios across the published reference range
schema.tier2_multiplier: Tier 2 lifestyle multiplier applied to the central [S]/Km ratio
schema.references: Verified citations / dataset identifiers backing the biomarker measurement or exposure proxy; these do not necessarily support target_enzyme or Km_uM
schema.source_status: Curated status describing whether the biomarker/range and enzyme/Km links are directly supported or model proxies
schema.provenance_note: Short note distinguishing direct biomarker evidence from model-normalization assumptions

references: CDC National Exposure Report PAH metabolites: urinary 1-hydroxypyrene, NHANES 2003-2010
CDC NHANES 2003-2004 OH-PAH urine lab method (1-hydroxypyrene)
PMID 23885861 Bouchard & Viau 1999 urinary 1-hydroxypyrene PAH biomonitoring review
PMID 12376124 Viau et al. 2002 dietary PAH/1-hydroxypyrene variability caveat
entries.provenance_note: Urinary 1-hydroxypyrene supports PAH/pyrene exposure, not CYP1A1-specific enzyme activity. CYP1A1 and Km_uM are retained as PAH activation normalization parameters from the flux model.

references: CDC NHANES 2003-2004 volatile organic compounds in whole blood lab method (blood benzene)
CDC National Exposure Report volatile organic compounds: blood benzene, NHANES biomonitoring tables
PMID 21989501 Aylward et al. 2011 NHANES VOC biomonitoring equivalents for blood benzene
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Benzene 2007
entries.provenance_note: Blood benzene supports benzene exposure. CYP2E1 and Km_uM are model-normalization parameters, not claims made by the NHANES VOC source.

references: CDC NHANES 2003-2004 cotinine in serum lab method
PMID 19019851 Benowitz et al. 2009 serum cotinine cutpoints in NHANES 1999-2004
PMID 10350520 Benowitz 1999 biomarkers of environmental tobacco smoke exposure
entries.provenance_note: Serum cotinine supports tobacco-smoke exposure. The TobaccoNitrosamines class assignment and CYP1A2 normalization are exposure-model proxies, not cotinine-specific enzyme evidence.

references: CDC NHANES 2007-2008 COTNAL_E tobacco-specific nitrosamines data file
PMID 21114376 Xia et al. 2011 urinary NNAL in smokers, NHANES 2007-2008
PMID 20833972 Bernert et al. 2010 urinary NNAL in the US population from secondhand smoke exposure
PMID 26678241 Hecht & Stepanov 2016 tobacco-specific nitrosamine exposure biomarkers
entries.provenance_note: Urinary NNAL supports NNK/tobacco-specific nitrosamine exposure. CYP2A13 and Km_uM are model-normalization parameters.

references: PMID 23101976 Cederbaum 2012 alcohol metabolism
NIAAA blood alcohol concentration and alcohol metabolism guidance
entries.provenance_note: Blood ethanol is treated as a scenario exposure proxy for moderate alcohol intake, not a NHANES biomarker range.

references: PMID 31504734 urinary ethyl glucuronide as a habitual alcohol-consumption biomarker
PMID 15289206 ethyl glucuronide as an alcohol-use biomarker
entries.provenance_note: Urinary ethyl glucuronide supports recent alcohol consumption. ALDH2 and Km_uM are aldehyde-flux normalization parameters.

references: PMID 23101976 Cederbaum 2012 alcohol metabolism
NIAAA blood alcohol concentration and alcohol metabolism guidance
entries.provenance_note: Blood ethanol is treated as a scenario exposure proxy for heavy alcohol intake, not a population biomarker range.

references: PMID 18616675 salivary acetaldehyde after alcohol by ALDH2 genotype
PMID 15239123 Salaspuro & Salaspuro 2004 alcohol/smoking salivary acetaldehyde
PMID 32775346 Salaspuro 2020 local acetaldehyde review
entries.provenance_note: Salivary acetaldehyde supports local acetaldehyde exposure after alcohol. ALDH2 and Km_uM are aldehyde clearance normalization parameters.

references: PMID 12351156 urinary PhIP metabolites after charbroiled or fried beef
PMID 12016157 urinary PhIP N2-glucuronide relationship to CYP1A2 and NAT2 activity
PMID 20681011 NIH-AARP meat components and bladder cancer
entries.provenance_note: Urinary PhIP supports heterocyclic amine exposure from cooked meat; the CYP1A2 link is supported at pathway/activity level, while Km_uM remains the model normalization value.

references: CDC National Exposure Report PAH metabolites: urinary naphthalene metabolites, NHANES biomonitoring tables
PMID 22436105 urinary 2-naphthol and PAH biomarker study
PMID 10511262 urinary 1-hydroxypyrene and other PAH metabolites biomarker review
entries.provenance_note: Urinary 2-naphthol supports naphthalene/PAH exposure, not CYP1A1-specific enzyme activity. CYP1A1 and Km_uM are PAH-class normalization parameters.

references: IARC Monographs Volume 114: Red meat and processed meat; N-nitroso compounds in processed meat
PMID 26514947 IARC Working Group 2015 carcinogenicity of red and processed meat
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for N-Nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) 2023
entries.provenance_note: Urinary_NDMA_equivalent is a processed-meat nitrosamine exposure proxy, not a directly validated single urinary biomarker row. CYP2E1 and Km_uM are NDMA activation normalization parameters.

references: OSHA benzene standard 29 CFR 1910.1028
PMID 15935803 urinary benzene metabolites in relation to genotype and personal exposure
PMID 12931845 validation and evaluation of benzene biomarkers in exposed workers
entries.provenance_note: Urinary trans,trans-muconic acid supports benzene exposure. CYP2E1 and Km_uM are benzene activation normalization parameters.

references: EPA IRIS Toxicological Review of Trichloroethylene 2011
EPA IRIS Toxicological Review of Trichloroacetic Acid 2011
PMID 20414643 urinary trichloroacetic acid as a biological exposure equivalent for trichloroethene
entries.provenance_note: Urinary trichloroacetic acid supports TCE exposure/metabolism. GSTT1 and Km_uM are chlorinated-solvent bioactivation normalization parameters.

references: CDC NHANES 2003-2004 urinary total and speciated arsenic data file
CDC NHANES 2003-2004 urine total arsenic lab method
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Arsenic 2007
entries.provenance_note: Urinary total arsenic supports arsenic exposure but includes organic seafood arsenicals unless speciated. AS3MT and Km_uM are inorganic-arsenic methylation normalization parameters.

references: PMID 16978023 quantification of AFB1-N7-guanine in human urine
PMID 17127712 urinary aflatoxin B1 exposure biomarker and hepatocellular carcinoma in Taiwan
PMID 19875698 Wild & Gong 2010 mycotoxins and human disease
entries.provenance_note: Urinary AFB1-N7-guanine supports biologically effective aflatoxin exposure. CYP3A4 and Km_uM are aflatoxin activation normalization parameters.
